<!-- conj-1: body_md -->
\label{conj:DHZ}
If $d\geq2$ and $X$ has a minimal complete-intersection embedding
in $\mathbb C^r$, with $r\geq d+1$, then $X$ admits a projective crepant
resolution.
<!-- end conj-1 -->
<!-- que-1: body_md -->
\label{que:IR-cohomology}
For a crepant resolution $Y\to{^{\textstyle \mathbb C^d}\big/_{\textstyle G}}$, with $d=4$ or $5$,
is the ordinary rational cohomology algebra $H^*(Y,\mathbb Q)$ generated
by $H^2(Y,\mathbb Q)$?
<!-- end que-1 -->
<!-- thm-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:CI-counterexamples}
The quotients in the following table are minimally embedded complete
intersections and have no projective crepant resolution. In
particular, they contradict Conjecture~\ref{conj:DHZ} in dimension four.
\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lrrrr@{}}
\toprule
Cases & $|G|$ & Generator degrees & Relation degrees & Embedding dimension\\
\midrule
\hyperlink{matrix-case-45}{45} & 36 & $2,2,6,6,6,6$ & $12,12$ & 6\\
\hyperlink{matrix-case-105}{105} & 24 & $2,2,4,5,5,6$ & $10,10$ & 6\\
\hyperlink{matrix-case-65}{65} & 288 & $2,6,8,12,12,12$ & $24,24$ & 6\\
\hyperlink{matrix-case-66}{66} & 576 & $2,6,8,12,24$ & $48$ & 5\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
<!-- end thm-1 -->
<!-- pro-1: body_md -->
\label{prop:cyclic-counterexample}
The quotient ${^{\textstyle \mathbb C^4}\big/_{\textstyle G_7}}$ admits a projective crepant
resolution, while $G_7$ contains a maximal cyclic subgroup without
junior elements.
Thus the necessary condition in \hyperlink{ce-02}{CE-02}, and hence both stronger
lattice conditions from which it follows, fail in dimension four.
<!-- end pro-1 -->
<!-- pro-2: body_md -->
\label{prop:cohomology-counterexamples}
For each of the following cases, every projective crepant resolution
has cohomology not generated by $H^2$. The last column gives a
lower bound for the number of further generators needed in degree four.
\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lrrrr@{}}
\toprule
Cases & $b_2$ & $b_4$ & $\binom{b_2+1}{2}$ & Deficit\\
\midrule
\hyperlink{matrix-case-35}{35}, \hyperlink{matrix-case-38}{38} & 2 & 4 & 3 & 1\\
\hyperlink{matrix-case-55}{55}, \hyperlink{matrix-case-98}{98} & 2 & 5 & 3 & 2\\
\hyperlink{matrix-case-64}{64} & 4 & 12 & 10 & 2\\
\hyperlink{matrix-case-97}{97} & 1 & 2 & 1 & 1\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
<!-- end pro-2 -->
<!-- def-1: body_md -->
A \emph{projective crepant resolution} of $X$ is a projective
birational morphism $f\colon Y\to X$ from a smooth variety such that
\[
 K_Y=f^*K_X.
\]
\emph{Here projectivity is relative to $X$; the variety $Y$ need
not be projective over $\mathbb C$.}
<!-- end def-1 -->
<!-- def-2: body_md -->
\label{def:age}
Let $g\in G$ have order $r$, and write its eigenvalues as
\[
 \exp\left(\frac{2\pi i a_1}{r}\right),\ldots,
 \exp\left(\frac{2\pi i a_4}{r}\right),
 \qquad 0\leq a_k<r.
\]
The \emph{age} of $g$ is
\[
 \operatorname{age}(g)=\frac{a_1+\cdots+a_4}{r}.
\]
An element is called \emph{junior} if its age is one. We denote by
\[
 J(G)=\langle g\in G:\operatorname{age}(g)=1\rangle
\]
the subgroup generated by all junior elements.
<!-- end def-2 -->
<!-- lem-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:real-age-short}
If $g$ is a real matrix of finite order with determinant one, acting
on $\mathbb C^4$, then
\[
 \operatorname{age}(g)=\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{rank}(g-I)
         =\frac{1}{2}\bigl(4-\dim V^g\bigr),
 \qquad V^g=\ker(g-I).
\]
In particular, $g$ is junior if and only if $\dim V^g=2$.
<!-- end lem-1 -->
<!-- thm-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:junior-generation}
Let $G\subset\operatorname{SL}(V)$ be finite. If ${^{\textstyle V}\big/_{\textstyle G}}$ admits a crepant
resolution, then $G$ is generated by its junior elements.
<!-- end thm-2 -->
<!-- def-3: body_md -->
\label{def:common-fixed-space}
The \emph{common fixed space} of the representation is
\[
 F=V^G=\{v\in V:gv=v\text{ for every }g\in G\}.
\]
If $g_1,\ldots,g_s$ generate $G$, then
\[
 F=\bigcap_{i=1}^s\ker(g_i-I).
\]
A \emph{fixed factor} is a nonzero subspace of $V^G$.
<!-- end def-3 -->
<!-- thm-3: body_md -->
\label{thm:maschke}
Let $G$ be a finite group acting on a finite-dimensional complex
vector space $V$. Every $G$-invariant subspace $F\subset V$ has a
$G$-invariant complement $W$, so that $V=F\oplus W$.
<!-- end thm-3 -->
<!-- pro-3: body_md -->
\label{prop:fixed-product}
With the notation above, the action of $G$ on $W$ is faithful and
has determinant one. Moreover,
\[
 \mathbb C[V]^G\simeq\mathbb C[F]\otimes_{\mathbb C}\mathbb C[W]^G,
 \qquad
 {^{\textstyle V}\big/_{\textstyle G}}\simeq F\times\left({^{\textstyle W}\big/_{\textstyle G}}\right).
\]
If $\pi\colon Y_W\to {^{\textstyle W}\big/_{\textstyle G}}$ is a projective crepant resolution,
then so is
\[
 \operatorname{id}_F\times\pi\colon F\times Y_W\longrightarrow {^{\textstyle V}\big/_{\textstyle G}}.
\]
<!-- end pro-3 -->
<!-- thm-4: body_md -->
\label{thm:low-dimensional-crepant}
Let $H\subset\operatorname{SL}_d(\mathbb C)$ be finite, with $d\leq3$. Then
${^{\textstyle \mathbb C^d}\big/_{\textstyle H}}$ admits a projective crepant resolution.
<!-- end thm-4 -->
<!-- cor-1: body_md -->
\label{cor:fixed-factor}
If $G\subset\operatorname{SL}_4(\mathbb C)$ is finite and $V^G\neq0$, then ${^{\textstyle V}\big/_{\textstyle G}}$
admits a projective crepant resolution.
<!-- end cor-1 -->
<!-- def-4: body_md -->
\label{def:quotient-lattice}
The \emph{quotient lattice} of this diagonal representation is
\[
 N=\mathbb Z^4+\sum_{g\in G}\mathbb Z\,\theta(g)\subset\mathbb Q^4,
 \qquad \theta(g)=(\theta_1(g),\ldots,\theta_4(g)).
\]
It contains $\mathbb Z^4$ with $|{^{\textstyle N}\big/_{\textstyle \mathbb Z^4}}|=|G|$. The determinant-one
condition makes $m_0(x)=x_1+x_2+x_3+x_4$ integral on $N$.
<!-- end def-4 -->
<!-- def-5: body_md -->
\label{def:junior-simplex}
The \emph{junior simplex} is the lattice simplex
\[
 \Delta=\{x\in\mathbb R_{\geq0}^4:m_0(x)=1\}
       =\operatorname{conv}(e_1,e_2,e_3,e_4)
\]
in the lattice $N$, where $e_1,\ldots,e_4$ are the standard basis
vectors. Its lattice points are the four vertices and the vectors
$\theta(g)$ for junior elements $g\in G$.
<!-- end def-5 -->
<!-- def-6: body_md -->
\label{def:triangulation}
A \emph{lattice triangulation} of $\Delta$ is a subdivision into
tetrahedra with vertices in $\Delta\cap N$, covering $\Delta$
and meeting along common faces. It is \emph{unimodular} if the
four vertices of every maximal tetrahedron form a basis of $N$.
Equivalently, for a matrix $M_T$ whose rows are these vertices,
\[
 |G|\,|\det M_T|=1.
\]
The triangulation is \emph{coherent} if there is a height function
$h\colon\Delta\cap N\to\mathbb R$ such that its maximal tetrahedra
are precisely the projections of the maximal lower faces of
\[
 \operatorname{conv}\{(v,h(v)):v\in\Delta\cap N\}.
\]
<!-- end def-6 -->
<!-- thm-5: body_md -->
\label{thm:toric-crepant}
If the junior simplex of a finite abelian group
$G\subset\operatorname{SL}_4(\mathbb C)$ admits a coherent unimodular triangulation,
then ${^{\textstyle \mathbb C^4}\big/_{\textstyle G}}$ admits a projective crepant toric resolution.
<!-- end thm-5 -->
<!-- def-7: body_md -->
\label{def:complex-reflection}
A \emph{complex reflection} on a complex vector space $\mathfrak h$
is an element $s\in\operatorname{GL}(\mathfrak h)$ of finite order with
$\operatorname{rank}(s-I)=1$. A finite subgroup $W\subset\operatorname{GL}(\mathfrak h)$ is a
\emph{complex reflection group} if it is generated by such elements.
Its representation is \emph{irreducible} if $\mathfrak h$ has no
nonzero proper $W$-invariant subspace.
<!-- end def-7 -->
<!-- def-8: body_md -->
\label{def:cotangent-representation}
The \emph{cotangent representation} associated with
$W\subset\operatorname{GL}(\mathfrak h)$ is the action on
$T^*\mathfrak h=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak h^*$ given by
\[
 w(x,\lambda)=(wx,\lambda\circ w^{-1}).
\]
In a basis of $\mathfrak h$ and its dual basis, its matrices are
\[
 \rho_{\mathrm{cot}}(w)=
 \begin{pmatrix}A_w&0\\0&A_w^{-\mathsf t}\end{pmatrix}.
\]
<!-- end def-8 -->
<!-- thm-6: body_md -->
\label{thm:cotangent-classification}
Let $W\subset\operatorname{GL}(\mathfrak h)$ be a finite irreducible complex
reflection group with $\dim\mathfrak h=2$. The quotient
${^{\textstyle \mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak h^*}\big/_{\textstyle W}}$ admits a projective crepant
resolution if and only if its reflection representation has type
\[
 W(A_2),\qquad G(m,1,2)\ (m\geq2),\qquad\text{or}\qquad W_4.
\]
<!-- end thm-6 -->
<!-- def-9: body_md -->
\label{def:complete-intersection-model}
A \emph{complete-intersection model} of $X$ is a presentation
\[
 \mathbb C[V]^G\simeq
 {^{\textstyle \mathbb C[z_1,\ldots,z_{4+c}]}\big/_{\textstyle (f_1,\ldots,f_c)}}
\]
in which $f_1,\ldots,f_c$ form a regular sequence: each $f_i$ is
a nonzerodivisor modulo its predecessors, and the generated ideal
is proper. In particular, $X$ is Gorenstein.
<!-- end def-9 -->
<!-- def-10: body_md -->
\label{def:ideal-blow-up}
For a nonzero ideal $I\subset R$, with $R$ an integral affine
coordinate ring, the \emph{blow-up} of $X=\operatorname{Spec} R$ in $I$ is
\[
 \operatorname{Bl}_I X=
 \operatorname{Proj}_R\Bigl(\bigoplus_{n\geq0}I^n\Bigr)\longrightarrow X.
\]
If $I=(a_0,\ldots,a_s)$, its nonempty $a_j$-chart has coordinate ring
\[
 R\left[\frac{I}{a_j}\right]
 =R\left[\frac{a_0}{a_j},\ldots,\frac{a_s}{a_j}\right]
 \subset R[a_j^{-1}].
\]
These charts glue to a projective birational morphism
\cite[II, \S7]{Hartshorne}.
<!-- end def-10 -->
<!-- pro-4: body_md -->
\label{prop:blowup-adjunction}
Let $X\subset M$ be a complete intersection in a smooth variety,
locally cut out by $f_1,\ldots,f_c$. Blow up a smooth centre of
codimension $r$ in $M$, with exceptional divisor $E$. Suppose
$X$ is not contained in the centre, and the divided transforms of
the $f_i$ cut out its strict transform $X'$ as a complete
intersection. If $m_i$ is the exceptional multiplicity of $f_i$
and $b:X'\to X$, then
\[
 \omega_{X'}\simeq b^*\omega_X\otimes
 \mathcal{O}_{X'}\bigl((r-1-\textstyle\sum_i m_i)E|_{X'}\bigr).
\]
Thus the step preserves the canonical sheaf when
$\sum_i m_i=r-1$.
<!-- end pro-4 -->
<!-- thm-7: body_md -->
\label{thm:complete-intersection-sieve}
Let $X$ be a normal Gorenstein fourfold, and let $f:Y\to X$ be
a composition of blow-ups of nonzero coherent ideal sheaves.
Suppose $Y$ is smooth. If there is a finite set $\Sigma\subset X$
such that $f$ is crepant over $X\setminus\Sigma$ and
\[
 \dim f^{-1}(x)\leq2\qquad\text{for every }x\in\Sigma,
\]
then $f$ is a projective crepant resolution.
<!-- end thm-7 -->
<!-- def-11: body_md -->
\label{def:double-cover}
Let $B$ be smooth, let $L$ be a line bundle on $B$, and let
$s\in H^0(B,L^{\otimes2})$ have reduced zero divisor $D$.
The associated \emph{double cover} is
\[
 \pi:X=\operatorname{Spec}_B(\mathcal{O}_B\oplus L^{-1})\longrightarrow B,
\]
where multiplication on $L^{-1}\otimes L^{-1}$ is given by $s$.
Locally it has equation $z^2=F$, where $F$ defines the
\emph{branch divisor} $D$. The cover is normal and Gorenstein, with
\[
 \omega_X\simeq\pi^*(\omega_B\otimes L).
\]
It is smooth precisely when $D$ is smooth, including the empty case.
<!-- end def-11 -->
<!-- pro-5: body_md -->
\label{prop:double-cover-discrepancy}
Let $b:B'\to B$ blow up a smooth irreducible centre $Z$ of
codimension $r\geq2$. Write $E$ for its exceptional divisor,
$m=\operatorname{mult}_Z D$ for the generic branch multiplicity,
and $D^{\mathrm{str}}$ for the strict transform. The normalization
$\pi':X'\to B'$ of the pulled-back cover has branch divisor
\[
 D'=D^{\mathrm{str}}+\left(m-2\left\lfloor\frac{m}{2}\right\rfloor\right)E
\]
and covering line bundle
$L'=b^*L\otimes\mathcal{O}_{B'}\left(-\left\lfloor\frac{m}{2}\right\rfloor E\right)$.
For the induced map $g:X'\to X$,
\[
 \omega_{X'}\simeq g^*\omega_X\otimes
 \pi'^*\mathcal{O}_{B'}\left(\left(r-1-\left\lfloor\frac{m}{2}\right\rfloor\right)E\right).
\]
<!-- end pro-5 -->
<!-- thm-8: body_md -->
\label{thm:double-cover-sieve}
Suppose $X={^{\textstyle \mathbb C^4}\big/_{\textstyle G}}$ has the double-cover presentation above.
If a sequence of admissible blow-ups of the base makes the updated
branch divisor a disjoint union of smooth divisors, then the final
normalized cover is a projective crepant resolution of $X$.
<!-- end thm-8 -->
<!-- cor-2: body_md -->
\label{cor:plane-branch-factors}
Let $B=\mathbb A^2\times\mathbb A^2$ and let $D$ be the sum of pullbacks of
reduced plane divisors. In each factor allow an empty divisor,
a line, two coordinate axes, a cusp $\alpha x^3-\beta y^2=0$
with $\alpha\beta\ne0$, or the two curves
\[
 y=\alpha x^k,\qquad y=\beta x^k,
 \qquad \alpha\ne\beta,\quad k\in\{1,2,3\}.
\]
Then the double cover admits a projective crepant resolution.
<!-- end cor-2 -->
<!-- def-12: body_md -->
The \emph{determinant extension} of $U$ is the representation
$V=\mathbb C_{\det}\oplus U$, where $\mathbb C_{\det}$ is the one-dimensional
representation with character $\det$. Thus
\[
 g(t,u)=(\det(g)t,gu),\qquad
 \rho_V(g)=\begin{pmatrix}\det(g)&0\\0&g\end{pmatrix}.
\]
In particular, $\rho_V(W)\subset\operatorname{SL}(V)$.
<!-- end def-12 -->
<!-- def-13: body_md -->
A fourfold has a \emph{transverse $A_1$ singularity} at a point if
its analytic germ there is the product of a smooth surface germ and
the surface singularity $ac=b^2$ at the origin.
<!-- end def-13 -->
<!-- lem-2: body_md -->
\label{lem:transverse-A1}
Let $Q$ be a normal fourfold whose singularities are transverse $A_1$
singularities. Then
\[
 \operatorname{Bl}_{\operatorname{Sing}(Q)_{\mathrm{red}}}Q
 \longrightarrow Q
\]
is a projective crepant resolution. In particular, this applies to
$Q={^{\textstyle M}\big/_{\textstyle \langle\iota\rangle}}$ if $M$ is a smooth fourfold and
the fixed locus of its nontrivial involution $\iota$ is a disjoint
union of smooth surfaces.
<!-- end lem-2 -->
<!-- thm-9: body_md -->
\label{thm:real-reflection-resolution}
There exists a projective ${^{\textstyle W}\big/_{\textstyle W^+}}$-equivariant crepant
resolution $R\to{^{\textstyle U}\big/_{\textstyle W^+}}$ for which the quotient of $R$ by
the residual involution $\sigma$ is smooth.
<!-- end thm-9 -->
<!-- thm-10: body_md -->
\label{thm:determinant-extension}
The quotient of a determinant extension of a real reflection
representation of dimension three admits a projective crepant resolution.
<!-- end thm-10 -->
<!-- def-14: body_md -->
Let $Z$ be a variety with involution $\overline\tau$. A resolution
$f\colon Y\to Z$ is \emph{equivariant} if there is an involution
$\tau_Y$ on $Y$ such that $f\circ\tau_Y=\overline\tau\circ f$.
Its fixed locus is $\operatorname{Fix}(\tau_Y)=\{y\in Y:\tau_Y(y)=y\}$.
<!-- end def-14 -->
<!-- pro-6: body_md -->
\label{prop:involution-fixed-locus}
Let $Y$ be a connected smooth fourfold with a nowhere-vanishing
four-form, and let $\tau_Y$ be a nontrivial involution preserving it.
Each component of $\operatorname{Fix}(\tau_Y)$ is either a smooth surface or an
isolated point. At a surface component the tangent eigenvalues are
$(1,1,-1,-1)$; at an isolated fixed point they are $(-1,-1,-1,-1)$.
<!-- end pro-6 -->
<!-- thm-11: body_md -->
\label{thm:toric-involution}
Suppose $f\colon Y_\Sigma\to{^{\textstyle \mathbb C^4}\big/_{\textstyle H_0}}$ is an
equivariant projective crepant toric resolution and the lifted
involution has no isolated fixed points. Set
\[
 Q={^{\textstyle Y_\Sigma}\big/_{\textstyle \langle\tau_Y\rangle}},\qquad
 \widetilde X=\operatorname{Bl}_{\operatorname{Sing}(Q)_{\mathrm{red}}}Q.
\]
Then $\widetilde X\to X$ is a projective crepant resolution.
<!-- end thm-11 -->
<!-- def-15: body_md -->
The \emph{Cox ring} of $Y_0$ is the class-graded algebra
\[
 R=\operatorname{Cox}(Y_0)=\bigoplus_{[D]\in L}H^0(Y_0,\mathcal{O}_{Y_0}(D)),
\]
with multiplication defined by a choice of divisor representatives
for a basis of $L$. Assume $R$ is finitely generated, and put
$\overline Z=\operatorname{Spec} R$ and $T=\operatorname{Hom}(L,\mathbb C^*)$.
The grading defines an action of the algebraic torus $T$ on $\overline Z$.
<!-- end def-15 -->
<!-- thm-12: body_md -->
\label{thm:cox-sieve}
Use the full Cox ring and its grading by the entire lattice $L$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item If $\chi$ belongs to the interior of a movable GIT chamber,
$U_\chi$ is smooth, and $T$ acts freely on $U_\chi$, then
$Y_\chi\to X$ is a projective crepant resolution.
\item Let $M\subset L_{\mathbb R}$ contain $\operatorname{Mov}(Y_0/X)$. Suppose finitely
many points $p_i\in\overline Z$ are singular or have nontrivial
$T$-stabilizer, and $M\subset\bigcup_i\omega(p_i)$.
Then $X$ has no projective crepant resolution.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end thm-12 -->
<!-- def-16: body_md -->
For a smooth surface $S$, its \emph{Hilbert square} $S^{[2]}$
parametrizes zero-dimensional subschemes of $S$ of length two.
The \emph{Hilbert--Chow morphism}
\[
 S^{[2]}\longrightarrow\operatorname{Sym}^2(S)={^{\textstyle S\times S}\big/_{\textstyle S_2}}
\]
sends a subscheme to its associated cycle.
If $S$ is symplectic, then $S^{[2]}$ is a smooth symplectic fourfold
and this morphism is projective and crepant.
<!-- end def-16 -->
<!-- pro-7: body_md -->
\label{prop:hilbert-fixed}
Let $S$ be a smooth quasi-projective symplectic surface with an
antisymplectic involution $\tau$. Then $\tau^{[2]}$ is antisymplectic
on $S^{[2]}$, and its fixed locus is a disjoint union of smooth
Lagrangian surfaces.
<!-- end pro-7 -->
<!-- thm-13: body_md -->
\label{thm:hilbert-square-tower}
Put $T=S^{[2]}$ and $\iota=\tau^{[2]}$. Then
\[
 Q={^{\textstyle T}\big/_{\textstyle \langle\iota\rangle}},\qquad
 Y=\operatorname{Bl}_{\operatorname{Sing}(Q)_{\mathrm{red}}}Q
\]
give a projective crepant resolution $Y\to X$.
<!-- end thm-13 -->
